d1269d8113: Security Audits of Genoryn Krypton: What Was Checked, and What Was Fixed
512364f8fc: Money is only as safe as the code behind it. Every part of Genoryn Krypton is reviewed again and again: the wallet, the swaps with bitcoin, the node, the rules of the chain, this website and the forum. Here is what each review checked, what it found, and how every finding was fixed.
05a2872445: Four reviewers, each in one area in depth: the swaps with bitcoin, the node and its network, the desktop wallet, and cryptography with the light client. Every finding was checked against the code; fixes that change what honest users see were tried on the real chain first.
cd8b5e7394: No way to mint GNR beyond the schedule
d8e35336e7: No way to spend someone else's GNR
4f736d9635: No way to break the privacy of transfers
11278d1ee0: No way to forge a block for a full node
292b400670: No consensus rule changed: every node and wallet keeps working with every other, and no coin or balance moves.
0924ad43d3: Four areas, each read line by line
65c3d7fdc0: Every step of a swap and every way it can end: restarts at any moment, deadlines, refunds racing claims, fees in a busy Bitcoin network, and a counterparty or Bitcoin server that does not behave.
9d1fe627f7: The peer-to-peer layer under load from many addresses, the node's API and its limits, the offer board and the messages it relays, the files it keeps, and the server configuration.
36d6e6cf4d: What a web page, another program or another user of the computer could do with it, the password on every action that matters, updates, and everything the window shows from the network.
88cda89418: What a dishonest node can make a light wallet believe, key derivation and randomness, note encryption, and the decoding of everything that comes from the network.
5d6e0ad59f: The full report on GitHub has each finding with its fix and its test. In short:
94e98f83e5: A dishonest node could get a light wallet to accept blocks nobody had worked for, with payments in them.
2cced59a66: Every block above the release checkpoint is checked as a full node checks it, and the chain must pass through the checkpoint.
9ec7846f81: One peer could slow a node's handling of every other peer's messages.
448b065ae6: Peers' transactions are checked outside the message loop, a few at a time and within a budget.
06fc63468c: A tiny payment could be made to show as a huge amount.
92f835c5b3: With the window's session token alone, a wallet could be added and made the one that receives payments and mining rewards.
0a938f1999: Adding a wallet needs the open wallet's password.
185258330e: Block announcements, bare connections and relayed swap messages from one place could crowd out everyone else.
a6275d7e02: Budgets per peer and client, room for new peers only after their handshake, and a daily quota of relayed message bytes.
1c639c55b7: The client address the node counts requests by came from a header only the firewall protected.
8299242aa0: It is taken from Cloudflare's header only when the request comes from Cloudflare.
aa3aae5eec: A seller could reveal the secret with little time left, and a claim waiting in a busy mempool got more fee only once.
bf9bb5aa5c: The secret is revealed only with ten blocks left, and the claim is signed again every block with more fee.
364907758a: On Linux and macOS, other users of the computer could read the window's session link.
488d12b695: The wallet's folder and files are for their user alone, and the link is no longer printed.
db9a7445b1: The work a node's tip claimed was remembered before its blocks were checked.
83cac3449a: Remembered only once every block up to it passed.
51dfec9dc5: Eleven issues: payment-proof confirmations, pending payments, note-tree data from nodes, board files, proofs of funds, mode and peer settings, a crashed wallet's link, the payment check of swaps, a finished seller's unclaimed GNR, unreadable swap records, and a deposit code that came before the lock.
50a2b6b7a3: All fixed; each one is in the full report.
1fc46962c0: Five smaller issues: response limits, frame protection, and arithmetic and checks with numbers from the other side of a swap.
442c70d7c0: All fixed, the arithmetic covered by property tests.
27fdecce5f: Findings that are still being worked on are not described until they are fixed, so that nobody can use them first. The findings of the 1.0.52 audit are in <0>its report</0>.
23a7d5af49: Swaps, node and network, desktop wallet, cryptography and the light client. 27 findings fixed in 1.0.53.
09134b1350: Full audit of the whole system
1f74cc325d: Wallet, swaps, Bitcoin signing, node and updates, consensus, website and forum. 30 findings fixed in 1.0.52.
d641cb2e2d: Private report by an independent researcher
e2cc95e552: Light-client chain selection, swap board authorization and smaller hardening items, reported privately and fixed in 1.0.33.
44e06915c3: Node and peer-to-peer layer, consensus and rewards, the wallets and light client, the website and server. Every fixable finding was fixed in 1.0.7.
96872ca5e2: The first review after launch, whose fixes every later review confirmed are still in place.
06e99ea74a: These are internal reviews, assisted by AI, and not a substitute for an audit by a specialised firm. Independent reviews are welcome, and every one will be published here.
3c15cff09b: Report vulnerabilities privately, never in public: you get an answer, a fix, and credit if you want it. Please never test against other people's coins or nodes.
